correctness.rationale: For a labeled configuration with k core and l peripheral ones, the fixed-state inequalities are k>0 ⇒2(k−1+l)≤a+b−1; k<a ⇒2(a−k−1+b−l)≤a+b−1; l>0 ⇒2k≤a; l<b ⇒2k≥a. For mixed core 0<k<a they imply a+b−1≤2(k+l)≤a+b+1. If k<a/2, peripheral zeros force l=b, contradicting 2k+b≤a+1 since b≥a and k≥1. If k>a/2, l=0 contradicts lower bound. Thus k=a/2 even, with l in the central one/two binomial layers; k=0 and k=a yield exactly two oppositely polarized states. Directly reimplemented all synchronous bit updates and compared every state against formula for all a<=5, a<=b<=8. Fixed-a b→∞ entropy follows from Stirling central binomial asymptotics; no claim on transient basins or b<a.
